lessons.title: Hello, panel
lessons.objective: Send one explicit text value to one explicit display sink.
lessons.prose: A panel is a bounded assembly of named nodes and cords. Run this one before changing it.
hints: The literal node produces text on its out port.
The stdout node consumes text on its in port.
lessons.solution: Connect greeting.out to output.in with the declared bounded cord.

accessibility.non_audio: The visible text output is the complete result.

lessons.title: Pull the cord

lessons.prose: Remove a cord on purpose. A useful diagnostic names the missing boundary instead of guessing a connection.
hints: The output node has one required input.
A node declaration does not create a connection.
lessons.solution: Restore the bounded cord from greeting.out to output.in.

lessons.title: Change the message
lessons.objective: Edit semantic configuration while preserving the same panel structure.
lessons.prose: Change the literal value, then select and move its faceplate. Source semantics and presentation are separate identities.
hints: Only the value configuration needs to change.
Moving a selected node does not rewrite source.

lessons.title: More than one port
lessons.objective: Patch two independently named inputs instead of treating a node like universal stdin.
lessons.prose: The display panel exports left and right jacks. Each jack retains its own typed boundary and each incoming cord has a separate finite budget.
hints: The exported names are display.left and display.right.
Each source needs its own cord.
lessons.solution: Connect left.out to display.left and right.out to display.right with separate bounded cords.

lessons.title: Direction matters
lessons.objective: See a wrong-direction cord rejected at the exact destination port.
lessons.prose: Ports are directional contracts. An output cannot stand in for an input, even when both nodes produce the same text type.
hints: Look at the port after the arrow.
A literal node only exposes an output port.
lessons.solution: Connect an output port to an input port, such as conduit.std/stdout.in.

accessibility.non_audio: The direction failure is exposed as a structured text diagnostic.

lessons.title: Fan-out is a choice
lessons.objective: Declare each consumer explicitly when one output feeds more than one sink.
lessons.prose: The literal output contract permits one or more connections. The two bounded cords are visible in source and each sink receives one value.
lessons.source:
panel 1

node greeting : conduit.std/literal {
    value = "Fan out.\n"
}
node first : conduit.std/stdout
node second : conduit.std/stdout

cord greeting.out -> first.in {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord greeting.out -> second.in {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
hints: The output node contract accepts more than one connection.
Each cord declares its own finite capacity and pressure rule.
lessons.solution: Keep two explicit cords from greeting.out, one to each sink input.

accessibility.non_audio: Both delivered values appear as text output.

runnability.reason: the current exact planner cannot bind repeated hosted implementation instances

lessons.title: Types mean promises
lessons.objective: See that naming an adapter does not make an absent contract or implementation real.
lessons.prose: Conduit never guesses a conversion. This source names an adapter that has not been declared or implemented, so resolution fails before execution.
lessons.source:
panel 1

node source : conduit.std/literal {
    value = "Adapt me.\n"
}
node adapter : example/text-adapter
node sink : conduit.std/stdout

cord source.out -> adapter.in {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord adapter.out -> sink.in {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
hints: The adapter name is not registered.
A real adapter needs its own contract and implementation.
lessons.solution: Replace the invented adapter with a declared compatible implementation, such as conduit.std/uppercase for this text exercise.

accessibility.non_audio: The missing implementation is reported as a structured text diagnostic.

lessons.title: Empty is not never
lessons.objective: Distinguish one empty value that completes from a live input that has produced nothing.
lessons.prose: This literal emits exactly one empty text value. The output is blank, but the finite run still completes with two terminal nodes and one conducted cord.
hints: Look at completion evidence, not only visible output.
The literal has an empty string value rather than no value.
lessons.solution: Keep one explicit empty literal connected to the sink and inspect the terminal evidence.

accessibility.non_audio: Completion is announced in text even though stdout is empty.

lessons.title: Put a panel in a panel
lessons.objective: Use a composite boundary as an ordinary typed transform node.
lessons.prose: The composite exports only the ports it chooses. Its internal uppercase worker remains an implementation detail while the boundary remains substitutable for a primitive node.
lessons.source:
panel 1

composite example/uppercase {
    node worker : conduit.std/uppercase
    export input in = worker.in
    export output out = worker.out
}

node source : conduit.std/literal {
    value = "boundary"
}
node transform : example/uppercase
node sink : conduit.std/stdout

cord source.out -> transform.in {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord transform.out -> sink.in {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
hints: The composite has an input export and an output export.
The top-level cords connect to the composite boundary, not directly to worker.
lessons.solution: Keep the worker behind exported in/out ports, then connect the literal to transform and transform to the sink.

accessibility.non_audio: The uppercase transformation is visible as text output and source structure.

lessons.title: The jacks on the front
lessons.objective: Expose only the internal ports that belong on a composite boundary.
lessons.prose: The internal worker remains private. The two exports are the complete public faceplate; outer cords cannot bypass it.
lessons.source:
panel 1

composite example/front-panel {
    node private_worker : conduit.std/uppercase
    export input text = private_worker.in
    export output result = private_worker.out
}

node source : conduit.std/literal {
    value = "jacks"
}
node faceplate : example/front-panel
node sink : conduit.std/stdout

cord source.out -> faceplate.text {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord faceplate.result -> sink.in {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
hints: Outer cords name faceplate.text and faceplate.result.
private_worker never appears in an outer endpoint.
lessons.solution: Export the private worker's input and output under public boundary names.

accessibility.non_audio: The public and private port names are available in source text.

lessons.title: Reuse without copying

lessons.prose: Both transforms share the same semantic definition. Their instance paths and runtime evidence remain distinct.
lessons.source:
panel 1

    node worker : conduit.std/uppercase
    export input in = worker.in
    export output out = worker.out
}

lessons.title: A tiny instrument
lessons.objective: Build a small reusable source panel with one explicit tick output.
lessons.prose: This deterministic metronome emits one finite tick. Later timing lessons will replace the fixture with an explicit clock contract rather than ambient wall time.
hints: The composite exports pulse.out as clock.tick.
The finite fixture does not read wall time.

lessons.title: Patchbay observes Patchbay
lessons.objective: Inspect the root patchbay.panel graph inside Patchbay itself.
lessons.prose: Patchbay is an authored .panel graph. Witness its composite surfaces (authoring, presentation, observation) and inspect its own logical and expanded topology.
lessons.source:
panel 1

composite patchbay/authoring {
    node editor : conduit.std/uppercase
    node parser : conduit.std/uppercase
    export input source_in = editor.in
    export output parsed_out = parser.out
    cord editor.out -> parser.in {
        capacity = 1
        max_value_bytes = 1024
        max_queued_bytes = 1024
        low_watermark = 0
        high_watermark = 1
        pressure = block
    }
}

composite patchbay/presentation {
    node layout : conduit.std/uppercase
    node canvas : conduit.std/uppercase
    export input positions_in = layout.in
    export output rendered_out = canvas.out
    cord layout.out -> canvas.in {
        capacity = 1
        max_value_bytes = 1024
        max_queued_bytes = 1024
        low_watermark = 0
        high_watermark = 1
        pressure = block
    }
}

composite patchbay/observation {
    node resolver : conduit.std/uppercase
    node evidence_feed : conduit.std/uppercase
    export input plan_in = resolver.in
    export output telemetry_out = evidence_feed.out
    cord resolver.out -> evidence_feed.in {
        capacity = 1
        max_value_bytes = 1024
        max_queued_bytes = 1024
        low_watermark = 0
        high_watermark = 1
        pressure = block
    }
}

node nav_selection : conduit.std/literal {
    value = "tour/meta-lesson\n"
}
node authoring_surface : patchbay/authoring
node presentation_surface : patchbay/presentation
node observation_surface : patchbay/observation
node console_sink : conduit.std/stdout

cord nav_selection.out -> authoring_surface.source_in {
    capacity = 4
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 4096
    low_watermark = 1
    high_watermark = 4
    pressure = block
}

cord authoring_surface.parsed_out -> presentation_surface.positions_in {
    capacity = 4
    max_value_bytes = 4096
    max_queued_bytes = 16384
    low_watermark = 1
    high_watermark = 4
    pressure = block
}

cord presentation_surface.rendered_out -> observation_surface.plan_in {
    capacity = 4
    max_value_bytes = 4096
    max_queued_bytes = 16384
    low_watermark = 1
    high_watermark = 4
    pressure = block
}

cord observation_surface.telemetry_out -> console_sink.in {
    capacity = 8
    max_value_bytes = 8192
    max_queued_bytes = 65536
    low_watermark = 1
    high_watermark = 8
    pressure = block
}
hints: Switch between Logical and Expanded topology to see Patchbay internals unfold.
Running executes the exact self-observation pipeline.
lessons.solution: Execute the patchbay.panel graph to observe Patchbay's own execution telemetry.

accessibility.non_audio: The self-observation results and topology projections are visible as text.
